title: Lesson 42 - Data migration governance: cutover planning, rollback, and post-go-live validation
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend appropriate techniques and methods for ensuring high data quality at load time and for governing the migration, including cutover planning, rollback, and post-go-live validation.

questions.question: A cutover's final delta sync is taking far longer than planned because change volume since the last sync was underestimated. What was missing?
options: A rehearsed, timed cutover runbook that measured the final delta sync realistically
questions.explanation: Only a rehearsed, timed runbook reveals realistic delta duration; batch size, duplicate rules, and archives do not address cutover timing.

questions.question: Which TWO are essential elements of a migration rollback plan?
options: Defined rollback triggers and authorized decision-makers
Immediate decommission of the legacy system at cutover
Keeping the legacy system available read-only for a viability window
questions.explanation: Rollback needs triggers/authority (A) and a read-only legacy window (C); immediate decommission (B) removes the rollback path and skipping validation (D) hides issues.

questions.question: Which activity belongs to post-go-live validation rather than pre-cutover?
options: Dry-run load in a full sandbox
Reconciling counts/aggregates and validating integrations and access after go-live
questions.explanation: Post-go-live validation reconciles counts, validates integrations, and checks access on the live system; profiling/ dry-run / mapping are pre-migration activities.
